coreLogic: Delegation chain: SLA::addGracePeriod resolves schedule then calls SlaGracePeriodCalculator::calculate in include/Services/SlaGracePeriodCalculator.php, which calls BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours in include/class.schedule.php (lines 475-485), which constructs BusinessHours and calls BusinessHours::addWorkingHours in include/class.businesshours.php (lines 87-183). Wall-clock fallback in SlaGracePeriodCalculator::calculate (lines 32-36) runs when $schedule is null or BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours returns false.
consumers: Ticket::getSLADueDate in include/class.ticket.php line 557 — sole direct call site of SLA::addGracePeriod; passes DateTime seeded from reopen date or create date in $cfg->getDbTimezone(), passes department schedule from $this->getDept()->getSchedule() as second argument, does not pass &$timeline; receives mutated DateTime, calls $dt->setTimezone($cfg->getDbTimezone()), returns formatted 'Y-m-d H:i:s' string or implicit null when SLA inactive/missing

Ticket::updateEstDueDate in include/class.ticket.php line 568 — indirect consumer via getSLADueDate(true) (bypasses est_duedate cache); assigns result to $this->est_duedate and persists via Ticket::save()
Ticket::getEstDueDate in include/class.ticket.php line 575 — indirect consumer via getDueDate() ?: getSLADueDate() for display and due-date comparisons
Ticket::clearOverdue in include/class.ticket.php line 2458 — indirect consumer via getSLADueDate(); nulls $this->est_duedate when SLA due datetime is in the past

Ticket::checkOverdue in include/class.ticket.php lines 4723-4743 — indirect consumer of persisted est_duedate (populated by updateEstDueDate chain); SQL filter est_duedate__lt NOW() triggers markOverdue(), does not call addGracePeriod directly
inputShape: Datetime $date (PHP object passed by value but mutated in place); optional BusinessHoursSchedule $schedule = null (resolved inside facade when null using precedence chain); optional array &$timeline = [] passed by reference for audit-log population on successful business-hours path. Grace period hours are NOT a parameter — read from $this->getGracePeriod() on the SLA instance.
outputShape: Always returns the same DateTime object reference passed as $date, mutated in place (never allocates a new DateTime). When the business-hours schedule path succeeds, &$timeline is populated with string audit entries copied from BusinessHours::getTimeline(). When no schedule resolves or schedule addWorkingHours returns false, falls back to wall-clock DateInterval addition (round(graceHours * 3600) seconds) on the same object. &$timeline is not populated on wall-clock fallback path.
sideEffects: Reads global $cfg in SLA::addGracePeriod for OsticketConfig::getDefaultSchedule() fallback when neither the argument schedule nor SLA::getSchedule() resolves

SLA::getSchedule() lazy-loads BusinessHoursSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getScheduleId()) database SELECT on first access when schedule_id is set, caching result on SLA::$_schedule instance property

OsticketConfig::getDefaultSchedule() lazy-loads BusinessHoursSchedule via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup($this->getDefaultScheduleId()) database SELECT when default schedule_id is set, caching on OsticketConfig::$defaultSchedule property
BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup() delegates to Schedule::parent::lookup() database SELECT filtered by Schedule::FLAG_BIZHRS
Reads SLA grace_period hours from SLA model instance property via $this->getGracePeriod() (loaded when SLA model was fetched)
SLA::addGracePeriod constructs a new SlaGracePeriodCalculator instance per call
SlaGracePeriodCalculator::calculate mutates input DateTime $date in place on schedule-success path via downstream addWorkingHours chain
SlaGracePeriodCalculator::calculate mutates input DateTime $date in place on wall-clock fallback path via $date->add(DateInterval) using round(graceHours * 3600) whole seconds

Populates caller &$timeline array by reference when schedule path succeeds: BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours assigns $timeline = $bhrs->getTimeline() after BusinessHours::addWorkingHours returns truthy
BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours constructs ephemeral BusinessHours($this) instance per call; no persistence of that object

BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours does not pass &$timeline into BusinessHours::addWorkingHours; audit strings accumulate on BusinessHours internal $timeline property and are copied to caller &$timeline only after success

BusinessHours::addWorkingHours reads Schedule::getNumEntries() which calls Schedule::getEntries() triggering ScheduleEntry::objects()->filter(['schedule_id' => $this->getId()]) database SELECT if entries are not cached on schedule
BusinessHours::addWorkingHours calls DateTime::setTimezone($this->getSchedule()->getDatetimeZone()) mutating input DateTime timezone to the schedule timezone
Schedule::getDatetimeZone() calls Schedule::getTimezone() which reads global $cfg via $cfg->getTimezone() when the schedule timezone field is unset
BusinessHours::initOccurrences resets BusinessHours instance $this->workhours and $this->holidays arrays to empty on each invocation inside the while loop
BusinessHours::initOccurrences clones input DateTime and, if the current date key is already in $this->workhours, advances clone by +1 day before scanning
BusinessHours::initOccurrences uses a fixed 72-hour grace_period_hrs window (default parameter) to bound occurrence scanning, independent of the SLA grace_period hours argument

BusinessHours::initOccurrences calls $this->getSchedule()->getEntries() and ScheduleEntry::getOccurrences($dt, $period->format('Y-m-d')) to populate the workhours occurrence map (database reads if entries uncached)

BusinessHours::initOccurrences calls $this->getSchedule()->getHolidaysSchedules() which lazy-loads each HolidaysSchedule via HolidaysSchedule::lookup($id) database SELECT, caching array on BusinessHoursSchedule::$holidays
Schedule::getHolidays() reads schedule configuration via Schedule::getConfiguration() -> Schedule::getConfig() -> new Config('schedule.'.$id)->getInfo() database read for holiday schedule id list
Holiday schedule entries loaded via HolidaysSchedule::getEntries() ScheduleEntry database SELECT for each linked holiday schedule

BusinessHours::addWorkingHours appends audit strings to BusinessHours::$timeline instance property via private timeline() method at start, partial-day apply, holiday-skip, day apply, backtrack, and final-datetime steps
BusinessHours::addWorkingHours mutates input DateTime in place via DateTime::modify() advancing to end of business day or holiday end time
BusinessHours::addWorkingHours mutates input DateTime in place via DateTime::sub(DateInterval) for backtrack when accumulated seconds exceed requested hours

Partial-day branch: when occurrence date key equals $date->format('Y-m-d') and ScheduleEntry::isAfterHours($date) is false and ScheduleEntry::isBeforeHours($date) is false, sets $partial=true and uses ScheduleEntry::diffTime($date) plus optional $leadtime instead of full ScheduleEntry::diff()
After-hours branch: when occurrence date key equals $date->format('Y-m-d') and ScheduleEntry::isAfterHours($date) is true, continues to next working day without adding time for that entry
Out-of-scope branch: when occurrence date key differs from current $date date and strtotime('$d '.$e->getEndsTime()) < $date->getTimestamp(), continues without adding time

Holiday branch: when $this->holidays[$d] is set, appends holiday-skip timeline entry, moves $date to holiday end via modify('$d '.$holiday->getEndsTime()), skips full-day holidays with continue, sets $partial=true and computes $leadtime as holiday-start minus business-day-start when holiday starts after business-day start
Backtrack branch: when $_seconds > $seconds after adding a day's time, subtracts intval(round($_seconds - $seconds)) seconds via DateInterval and breaks the foreach loop

When grace_period hours is zero or non-numeric, BusinessHours::addWorkingHours returns $date immediately without adding time (truthy return), so SlaGracePeriodCalculator returns early without wall-clock fallback

When schedule has zero entries, BusinessHours::addWorkingHours returns false causing BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours to return false and SlaGracePeriodCalculator to fall through to wall-clock fallback
No database writes anywhere in SLA::addGracePeriod, SlaGracePeriodCalculator::calculate, BusinessHoursSchedule::addWorkingHours, or BusinessHours::addWorkingHours call chain
constraints: Schedule resolution precedence in addGracePeriod: caller-provided BusinessHoursSchedule argument, then SLA::getSchedule(), then global $cfg->getDefaultSchedule() (PHP elvis ?: is left-associative: ($schedule ?: $this->getSchedule()) ?: $cfg->getDefaultSchedule())
Grace period magnitude read from SLA model grace_period field via getGracePeriod() in hours, not passed as a method parameter
addGracePeriod does not call BusinessHours::addWorkingHours directly; only via $schedule->addWorkingHours() on the resolved BusinessHoursSchedule
If a schedule resolves but addWorkingHours returns false (empty schedule entries), addGracePeriod falls through to wall-clock grace addition rather than returning early
Wall-clock fallback uses round(grace_period * 3600) whole seconds via DateInterval, not business-hours arithmetic
Input DateTime is always mutated in place; callers must not assume immutability or a new object reference
$timeline audit log populated only when the schedule business-hours path succeeds; not populated on wall-clock fallback path
Ticket::getSLADueDate passes department schedule from $this->getDept()->getSchedule() as explicit schedule argument (Dept lazy-loads via BusinessHoursSchedule::lookup before addGracePeriod call)
Ticket::getSLADueDate seeds DateTime from reopen date if set else create date, in $cfg->getDbTimezone(), before calling addGracePeriod
Ticket::getSLADueDate calls $dt->setTimezone($cfg->getDbTimezone()) after addGracePeriod returns before formatting to string
Ticket::getSLADueDate returns cached $this->est_duedate without calling addGracePeriod when $recompute is false and est_duedate is set

Overdue detection consumes persisted est_duedate (derived from addGracePeriod output) not addGracePeriod directly: Ticket::checkOverdue SQL filter on est_duedate__lt NOW(), Ticket::clearOverdue compares getSLADueDate() to current time
harnessInputShape: JSON object with: start (string, ISO 8601 datetime); hours (number, grace period hours — use 0 for guard cases); schedule_id (integer, BusinessHoursSchedule id — 1 for normal business-hours schedule, 5 for empty-schedule fallback testing)
